newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Rugby Union-Australia competition set to start in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Rugby Union-Australia competition set to start in 1998.

text.p: The Australian Rugby Union (ARU) has set its sights on launching a national club competition in 1998 after ruling out an earlier kick-off as unfeasible.
The proposed start for the competition has been put back 12 months from 1997 because of disagreements within the game about its format and timing, the ARU announced.

"It was agreed that a National Competition in 1997 was not possible, however it was unanimously resolved that the creation of such a competition was imperative for 1998," ARU chief executive officer John O'Neill said.
The ARU said it will establish a working party, including players' representatives and members of the various state unions, to develop the concept.
O'Neill said the clubs were split over whether the competition should feature composite sides or existing clubs.
The timing of the competition also proved a stumbling block after the ARU ruled it must not disrupt the existing club competition in Sydney.
One thing was agreed -- the national competition must feature a reasonable number "star quality" players of Super 12 standard, the ARU said.
